newsitem.title: GERMANY: Holzmann says senior executive detained.
newsitem.headline: Holzmann says senior executive detained.

text.p: German building firm Philipp Holzmann AG on Wednesday confirmed that the chief executive of one of its units had been detained by police in Munich but could not confirm he was being held on suspicion of corruption.

The Munich state prosecutors' office had earlier told Reuters that the Holzmann executive, Dieter Schneider, had been held since Friday on suspicion of fraud and bribery "connected with building plans in the underground train sector."
"I can only confirm that he was detained," a spokesman for Holzmann said.

He added that he did not yet know what Schneider was suspected of, but had the impression that the case concerned the executive's activities before he became chief executive of Philipp Holzmann Bau-AG Sued in autumn 1995.
In Munich, prosecutors declined to make any further comment on the case at present. More information may be released in the middle of next week.
